text: Planning is done. This is the first lesson where Snowflake actually opens -- we're standing up the warehouse and the raw landing database.
An extra-small virtual warehouse and a dedicated raw database, with auto-suspend so we're never paying for idle compute between nightly runs.
The raw landing tables use permissive VARCHAR columns plus load metadata -- a malformed value from SQL Server should land successfully here, not reject the whole nightly file.
Before Airflow ever touches this on a schedule, we prove the path by hand: files into the stage, COPY INTO the raw tables, then a row-count check against the source export.
Raw data is landing in Snowflake. Next: building the actual dbt staging models on top of it.
